text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed ~1.6k reconnects/min for SSE in eu-west around 02:14–02:16. Console shows reconnect_count spike but resume_count stayed flat. tagging eng-platform
kevin: I see it in proxy logs too — lots of 499/connection_reset then immediate reconnects. Could be idle timeout + client-side retry loop.
sam: Which panel are you looking at? reconnect vs resume mismatch is the confusing bit for folks.
maria: The panel is plotting streaming_reconnect_total vs stream_resume_success_total. They should be correlated. This divergence looks like the proxy is closing before resume handshake can happen.
lee: Any tenant/route scoped?
maria: Tenant T-42 only. Timeline aligns with a canary rollout of the "graceful_backoff" flag from console at ~02:10.
kevin: Wait — that flag changes how we close idle streams, right? We returned 204 previously? If proxy treats 204 as normal response, it might short-circuit resume semantics.
sam: Can you paste the rollout config?
maria: Sure, from the rollout config:```
routing:
  streaming:
    graceful_backoff:
      enabled: true
      idle_timeout_ms: 20000
      close_code: 204
```
kevin: 204 is ambiguous for proxies (envoy maps to OK). If the gateway sees a 204 it might not mark it as a streaming EOF, so clients re-open but without resume token exchange.
lee: Telemetry I ran quickly: `sum by (tenant) (increase(streaming_reconnect_total[5m]))` -> T-42 shows a huge jump. `increase(stream_resume_success_total[5m])` is tiny.
maria: That matches. Clients are reconnecting but not performing successful resume (so higher duplicate token usage and intermittent 429s).
sam: UX/console note: the dashboard stacks these metrics but the tooltip doesn't explain close_code vs resume semantics. We should surface that. Users are confused when reconnect > resume.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for feature/graceful_backoff started 02:09 — 1/3 nodes updated, completed 03/3 at 02:11.
kevin: Quick mitigation options: (A) revert the flag for T-42; (B) change close_code to a 4xx that proxies treat as socket close; (C) add an explicit header `x-stream-close: idle` so proxies and telemetry can disambiguate.
lee: I prefer (C) + telemetry: emit `stream_close_reason` tag and increment `stream_close_reason_total{reason="graceful_backoff"}` so dashboards can break it down. Also add circuit-breaker to stop resume storms.
maria: I'll revert the flag for T-42 now and re-run a canary. Filing ENG-3421 to track.
sam: Dashboard action: add tooltip + new panel that shows `stream_close_reason_total` and a ratio card for reconnects/resumes. Also add alert: `reconnect_count > 2 * resume_count for 1m` to catch regressions.
kevin: I'll open a PR to change rollout to set `x-stream-close: idle` and keep status 499 for now until proxy behavior is clarified. Will ping ops for an urgent proxy rule review.
maria: Thanks — after revert I'll post a short summary in #incidents if the revert stabilizes.
kevin: :thumbsup:
sam: I'll own dashboard changes and alert.
lee: I'll add the new metric instrumentation and a PromQL example in the issue. Proposed promql: `sum by (tenant, reason)(increase(stream_close_reason_total[5m]))`
maria: Action items: maria -> revert canary for T-42; kevin -> PR for header+status; sam -> dashboard tooltip/alert; lee -> instrument close_reason metric. tagging @oncall for visibility.
kevin: Noted. Will update ENG-3421 with timeline and logs.
maria: Closing loop here once revert confirmed stable. Thanks everyone.
